key_points.point_text: Central thesis: proposers systematically end up with better outcomes than receivers, and this is not because of talent, luck, or the quality of their choices.
key_points.evidence_quote: Better outcomes come from whether one proposes or receives, not talent or luck.
key_points.reasoning: L003 states the thesis and explicitly excludes talent and luck; L002 frames it as systematic. Meaning intact.

key_points.point_text: In 1962 mathematicians-economists David Gale and Lloyd Shapley worked on creating stable pairings between two groups and proved a stable matching (no unmatched pair preferring each other) always exists.
key_points.evidence_quote: In 1962 Gale and Shapley sought pairings no unmatched pair would break.
key_points.reasoning: Year 1962, names, and the stability definition (no unmatched pair would break) survive, but the dropped condition that they proved a stable matching always exists is a key result. Per the rule on dropped conditions, capped at Partial.

key_points.point_text: Their deferred acceptance algorithm works by having one side propose in order of preference while the other side accepts or tentatively rejects based on its preferences.
key_points.evidence_quote: Deferred acceptance gives each proposer their best stable partner, each receiver their worst.
key_points.reasoning: Deferred acceptance is named, but the actual mechanism (one side proposes down its preference list, the other tentatively accepts/rejects) is never described. A new reader learns the outcome but not how the algorithm runs, so the point is narrowed.

key_points.point_text: Core mathematical result: proposers each get their best possible stable partner and receivers each get their worst possible stable partner, a provably extreme gap, not a slight difference.
key_points.evidence_quote: The gap is systematically, provably, mathematically extreme, not slight.
key_points.reasoning: L005 gives best-for-proposer / worst-for-receiver and L006 preserves the provable-extremity qualifier and the not-slight contrast.

key_points.point_text: Most real-world situations do not follow the exact algorithm but share the same proposer/receiver structure, so the same pattern of advantage should be expected even when only approximate.
key_points.evidence_quote: Real situations skip the exact algorithm but share the propose-respond structure.
key_points.reasoning: L007 captures both halves: departure from the exact algorithm and retention of the propose-respond structure, from which the shared pattern follows.

key_points.point_text: Everyday illustrations show most people are receivers: choosing Netflix by scrolling, picking among displayed phones, applying to posted jobs, accepting friendships formed by proximity.
key_points.evidence_quote: Netflix, phones, jobs, friendships: pre-decided pursuit versus presented selection.
key_points.reasoning: L008 lists all four domains and L009 states that most of us are receivers in these cases.

key_points.point_text: The insidious part is that receivers get acceptable, good-enough outcomes, so they never feel dissatisfied enough to change, and the system stays stable (self-sustaining) while quietly giving them less than they could have.
key_points.evidence_quote: Fine feelings block revolt-driving dissatisfaction; quiet under-service stays stable.
key_points.reasoning: L010 gives good-enough outcomes, L011 distinguishes decent from best-serving, L012 supplies the stability trap and suppressed dissatisfaction.

key_points.point_text: Chicken-and-egg trap: you need intention to propose, but you develop intention through proposing; choosing among presented options only reveals what you dislike least, not what you would pursue.
key_points.evidence_quote: Intention is needed to propose, yet intention develops only through proposing.
key_points.reasoning: L013 states the circular dependency and L014 preserves the least-disliked versus freely pursued desire distinction.

key_points.point_text: Training ground: the muscle of intention builds progressively, so start small by intentionally deciding what you want from the next hour before opening any app, rather than scrolling until something catches you.
key_points.evidence_quote: Tonight: name the hour's want (laugh, learn, calm, challenge), then seek it.
key_points.reasoning: L016 gives progressive muscle-building and no-jump scope; L017 gives the concrete hour-level small start with pre-decision.

key_points.point_text: You cannot think your way into values, you have to practice your way into them: repeated intentional acts yield patterns, patterns become preferences, preferences become values.
key_points.evidence_quote: Patterns become preferences, preferences values; values are practiced into, not thought into.
key_points.reasoning: L018 carries the full chain and the explicit practiced-into / not-thought-into contrast.

key_points.point_text: Structural disadvantage does not disappear with understanding, you must actually switch positions, and proposing means deciding what you want before seeing options, pursuing specifics, creating opportunities, and accepting friction against default flows.
key_points.evidence_quote: Propose: decide before seeing options, pursue specifics, create openings, accept friction.
key_points.reasoning: L023 preserves that understanding changes nothing absent an actual position switch against defaults; L024 lists all four proposal behaviors.

key_points.point_text: Collective effect: when most people are receivers, systems optimize for the proposers, namely the platforms, which capture optimal outcomes (attention, data, money) while users get only good-enough outcomes.
key_points.evidence_quote: Platforms take optimal outcomes (attention, data, money); users keep good-enough engagement.
key_points.reasoning: L020 establishes proposers winning from structural position; L021 gives the platform extraction with all three currencies and the good-enough user outcome.

key_points.point_text: Most people will not make the shift because it is effortful, the receiver position is comfortable, and after years of receiver mode many have lost the capacity to know what they would want to propose.
key_points.evidence_quote: Most will refuse: effortful, comfortable, and forgetful of what to propose.
key_points.reasoning: L026 lists all three barriers: effort, comfort, and lost capacity to know what to propose.

key_points.point_text: Practical progression: begin with tomorrow morning before checking your phone, practice for a week on small things (breakfast, evening activities, weekend plans), then scale to bigger decisions like work, relationships, and purchases.
key_points.evidence_quote: Start tomorrow morning small, practice a week, then scale to big decisions.
key_points.reasoning: L028 gives the staged progression, L029 the morning-before-phone start, and L030 the week-long small practice scaling to work, love, and problems.

key_points.point_text: Appendix concrete tools: domain exercises (entertainment, shopping with must-haves and 24-hour rule over $100, career with 5 non-negotiables and applying only when 4 of 5 match, relationships), daily pause and journaling practices, and a 30-day tracking journal showing proposers report higher satisfaction.
key_points.evidence_quote: Shopping drill: exact problem, 3-5 must-haves, 24-hour rule over $100 ... Jobs drill: five non-negotiables, apply only at 4-of-5 matches.
key_points.reasoning: L032-L035 cover all four domain drills with their retained numbers, L036 the micro-practices, and L037 the 30-day three-column journal.
